- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model still holds high forecast; adjust downward by 1–4% per day of lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts; apply smoothing or sentiment-weighted average to forecast.
